Slides, dashboards and documents people share are often the part of a meeting you most want to look back on. With "Capture shared screens"... Granola can take screenshots of what's being presented and attach them to your note.

Granola terrifies me. It’s highly capable at summarisation, and seems to be free. What’s the catch? ... it runs in the background on my Mac, has access to my microphone, my calendar data and my private meeting notes, that is potentially very scary indeed.
I just can’t bring myself to try out ANOTHER meeting notetaker app. The space just feels so commoditised. How different will this be to Fireflies? Or the six dozen others?
They're going to enshittify when they run out of money or sell your data. I also think automatic meeting transcription is potentially kind of bad for us... why not have everyone write an email?
It's free for a limited number of notes. I guess you could copypaste the note summaries out to Obsidian or something, but at that point you're better off using MacParakeet, OpenWhispr, etc.
I've been beta testing it and it seems like it's not bad for battery life at all, works like a charm.
pretty dope product - but who are these things made for? if most companies are forcing people to attend meetings in person - are people recording in-person meetings?

I work as a PM and have a lot of calls and action items that tend to slip through so I've built a Mac app that turns Granola calls into a kanban to-do list... For me privacy is important so all the data stays on my local device as .md files.
